seo.title: gravity.integration technology — more than an ESB
seo.description: Four in-house technologies behind gravity.integration: Always-on-data, firstSIGNAL, IntelliChain and Powers AI. An ESB that runs 24/7 and feeds data to AI.
seo.focusKeyword: next-generation ESB, AI-ready ESB, enterprise service bus

sections.text:
gravity.integration leaves ESBs in the previous era

gravity.integration is world-class Enterprise Service Bus (ESB) software, built for integrating other software.
So much for the theory. In practice, gravity.integration is a unique product that can do a great deal more. It grew out of our 20 years of experience building enterprise-class ERP software. In 2020 we saw the need for better information exchange between our own systems and the third-party solutions our customers ran — but the products on the market were limited and far too expensive.

So we decided to build that software ourselves — and since we don't do half measures, what we're putting in your hands is an exceptional product that we use every day and consider the best in its class. Not without reason.

Watch the video
In a world where everything is connected, how you connect is everything.

Tomorrow's tools

in your hands today. Meet the technologies developed at Caffeine Minds that let us say gravity is more than an ESB.

boxes.text:
Always-on-data

The only data bus that works even when you don't have to. gravity.integration keeps processing data through idle periods, so it can raise an event on its own the moment one is needed.

Powers AI, AI powered

Ready today for the solutions of tomorrow: gravity.integration delivers excellent-quality data for machine learning and is built to take that knowledge back in.

firstSIGNAL

gravity.integration is not just an exceptional tool for developers — it is a real advantage in business. A well-programmed bus can announce events before they ever reach the target system.

IntelliChain

Building integrations has never been this simple! The construct we call the intelligent chain doesn't just speed up the integration itself — it makes later changes trivially easy.
